quarterly_data.quarter: Onto Innovation Citi’s Global TMT Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CEO Mike Plisinski said the growth Onto has implied is around 40%, significantly above its peers and nearly double its peers, and that rather than trying to pull upside into Q3 or Q4 the focus is on driving additional backlog for 2027, making sure the supply chain ramps effectively and quality is maintained. On the share question at the customer where Onto had lost position, he said 'did we gain it all back, for sure', noted Onto said back in March it was qualified for all, that the customer has been factory constrained and did not spend a ton, and that Onto received huge OSAT orders; where the allocations actually land will be seen when that customer starts spending more aggressively in 2027, and that customer tends to care more about total spend with a supplier than about second-sourcing on a per-layer basis. The competitor is already reacting and trying to fight back.
quarterly_data.figure: implied growth around 40%, nearly double our peers

quarterly_data.quarter: Onto Innovation Citi’s Global TMT Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Dragonfly G5 strategy clarified: management does NOT expect a G3-to-G5 transition. Customers still appreciate the G3 for its lower price point, and for ClearFind/subsurface or 3DI applications the G5 platform gives no added benefit so those stay on G3, which has been growing phenomenally throughout 2026. The G5 is instead about expanding into NEW markets - high resolution, 100 nm type inspection applications in the front end plus several specialty device applications - which is the focus for 2027. Onto had about 10 customers across 15 different applications a quarter ago and expects, based on evaluation feedback, that the majority of those will convert to orders throughout 2027. CFO Brian Roberts confirmed the G5 is margin accretive with a better ASP and a better margin profile.
quarterly_data.figure: about 10 customers across 15 different applications; majority expected to convert to orders throughout 2027

quarterly_data.quarter: Onto Innovation Citi’s Global TMT Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: A new growth leg is forming in power semiconductors from data center power. Onto's earlier power-semi run was driven not by capacity expansion but by customers using Onto's inspection and metrology to drive yield improvement, with yields in the 60%-70% range rather than the 90s. The EV recovery has not really happened yet, but those same customers are now telling Onto they see demand from data centers driving adoption of power semiconductors and that Onto needs to prepare. Management is not seeing the actual orders yet and has no good clarity on timing, but said 2027 into 2028 is what the customers are thinking about; because the process control is already inserted in their process, Onto should benefit as they expand. Data center power is relatively small for Onto today and would be captured under specialty devices.
quarterly_data.figure: yields in the 60%-70% range; customers thinking 2027 into 2028

quarterly_data.quarter: Onto Innovation Citi’s Global TMT Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CFO Brian Roberts on the margin path and supply: 2026 margin gains have come from operational productivity and the move of manufacturing from the U.S. to the international extended factories - a year ago Onto was shipping its first tools from those factories and in Q2 it shipped about 70% of its tools from them. To date Onto has driven 250 basis points of gross margin and doubled that at the operating margin line. Into 2027, the accretive Dragonfly G5 and Atlas G6 add ASP lift which, alongside productivity, drives toward 'a margin that starts with a six'. The two major 2026 headwinds were memory cost and freight/fuel shortage, partly offset by being in region, and Onto is having pricing conversations with customers about the existing product portfolio for the 2027 pricing/budgeting season. On supply, the extended-factory move gave Onto partner capacity and new clean rooms without heavy CapEx; the supply chain is not perfect but Onto is using customer visibility to get ahead of bottlenecks, is carrying a higher inventory balance, is not missing customer dates and its lead times have not grown too much.
quarterly_data.figure: about 70% of tools shipped from international factories in Q2; 250 basis points of gross margin to date; target gross margin that starts with a six

quarterly_data.quarter: Onto Innovation Citi’s Global TMT Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management explained what sits behind the >$200 million single-OSAT Dragonfly order: with the industry constrained on heterogeneous integration, end customers are looking at alternative packaging technologies (EMIB among them), and separately 'TSMC is well-publicized. TSMC is looking at how to release more capacity' given fab constraints - taking its lower-end process steps and outsourcing those to the OSATs to free precious fab capacity for the higher end. Plisinski said that dynamic was in play in the order, and that OSAT capital intensity is really volume-driven, with the volume expected to come both from that outsourced capacity and from the OSATs' own technology that they will be selling. On share at the OSATs versus the foundries, Onto has very high share on the 2D side at the higher-end applications and has gained nice traction on 3D bump metrology at at least a couple of the OSATs; share is lower in low-end or China work.

quarterly_data.quarter: Onto Innovation Citi’s Global TMT Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Growth split disclosed: this year the biggest growth was in packaging at 80% growth while advanced nodes was about 35% growth, and for next year management expects not those numbers but similar dynamics, with advanced packaging still probably growing stronger than advanced nodes and both growing fairly well. Within advanced packaging the memory (HBM) versus 2.5D logic mix is fairly well split, generally around the 50/50 mark or 60/40 depending on the quarter, because logic requires the memory around it so the whole packaging requirement grows across both. On share, Onto has always had very high share in memory and maintained it, with incremental gains tied to 3D bump metrology as bumps get smaller and denser (3DI); in logic packaging there is room to gain share because of the very high resolution the Dragonfly G5 provides.
quarterly_data.figure: packaging 80% growth vs advanced nodes about 35% growth; advanced packaging memory/logic mix around 50/50 to 60/40

quarterly_data.quarter: Onto Innovation Citi’s Global TMT Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: First sizing of the panel-level packaging opportunity: Plisinski said Onto has publicly put the market at around a $1 billion SAM (competitors have said even more), covering process control - inspection as well as lithography - and that while Onto will not get 100% of it against competitors, '$200 million, $300 million' would be a reasonable expectation over the next few years. The accelerant is that constraints in AI packaging and heterogeneous integration are pushing customers to panel as an alternative: as die and therefore packages get bigger the economies of scale at the wafer level stop working - at 310 by 310 they get better, but that is still much smaller than 600 by 600 or 510 by 515 - so customers are moving capacity to companies with a proven process that can ramp right now. Adoption is still early and management expects it to continue over the next several years. The enterprise-server driver (advanced IC substrates, where Intel and AMD were constrained during COVID) is also working its way back, addressed by the JetStep X500 and Firefly.
quarterly_data.figure: around a $1 billion SAM; Onto share expectation $200 million, $300 million over the next few years

contracts.source: Onto Innovation Citi’s Global TMT Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
contracts.signal: Plisinski confirmed the Rigaku transaction has closed ('First it's closed, so that's done deal') and declined to discuss further steps. He said the partnership is strategic not because OCD is running out of steam - Onto believes it can keep pushing OCD for the foreseeable future - but because as the world moves to more 3D transistors and 3D stacking of die or wafers there are elements between layers that optical cannot solve, where X-ray can see through. Onto has already started with two different customers, went up against the leading player in X-ray and beat them at both customers, on the strength of Onto's AI Diffract modelling engine combined with Rigaku's sensor/X-ray capability. The next step is hybrid metrology - the speed of optical combined with the precision of slower X-ray - made simpler because AI Diffract already aggregates and models the data streams together.

quarterly_data.quarter: Onto Innovation Citi’s Global TMT Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: On the silicon photonics opportunity split, management said inspection will for sure be the largest opportunity and that this is reflected in the backlog Onto holds now - the bulk is inspection - but Onto is also selling metrology tools with multiple customers adopting a couple of different metrology tools, and sees opportunities for other tools in the space too. On what drives upside or downside to the opportunity, Plisinski said it is not a question of if it happens but how quickly the technology is adopted at the server level and then at the rack level, with Onto playing in both; he cited NVIDIA, Broadcom and AMD as committed to driving it forward and the hyperscalers as committed from a data center perspective, with everyone convinced on the economics and performance benefits. Silicon photonics is also one of the named drivers behind Onto's expectation that it can outperform the market in 2027, alongside the Dragonfly G5 opening front-end markets and Atlas G6 logic expansions.
